implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 1 — FORGERY, and the rule that makes it mean anything. Create `tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts`. This axis is about digests, codecs and authority records, so the central hostile move is a forged-but-internally-consistent payload.
EVERY FORGERY CASE MUST RESEAL THROUGH THE PRODUCTION CODEC. Mutate the field under test, then RE-DIGEST and RE-ENCODE through the same production path that seals a genuine record, so the payload passes its own integrity check and only the SUBJECT is wrong. A probe that mutates a field without resealing tests the digest check and nothing else — it would pass against an implementation with no subject binding at all, which is precisely the defect these boundaries exist to catch.
Assert BOTH halves per forgery: that the forged payload PASSES the digest/shape check (proving the reseal worked and the case is not a mismatch in disguise), and that it is then REFUSED on the subject with the exact code and layer.
SUBJECTS TO FORGE, per boundary: a configuration manifest whose settings digest is resealed over different bytes (PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CODEC_LAYERS, PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS, PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION_LAYER); a session credential resealed for a different principal or project (SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS, SESSION_AUTHORITY_DAEMON_LAYERS); an approval resealed against a different subject or graph revision (APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS, CORE_APPROVAL_LAYER); a recovery completion digest resealed over a different coverage set (RECOVERY_COMPLETION_LAYER); a reducer input resealed for a different project (PROJECT_REDUCER_LAYER); a review decision resealed for a different round or subject (REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS); a distribution or document-work proposal resealed for a different target (DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_LAYERS, DOCUMENT_WORK_PROPOSAL_LAYERS); and for RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_LAYER, a key-epoch proof resealed against a different epoch.
SECRETS RULE, binding on this axis specifically: no test may assert on, log, or embed key material, a credential value or a raw secret — assert on digests and refusal codes only. A test that prints a credential to prove it was rejected has published it.
implementationPlan.note:
FORGERY ARM LANDED, RESEALED THROUGH PRODUCTION, ASSERTED IN TWO HALVES.

STRUCTURE mirrors the sibling transport slice (its untracked `transport-boundaries.security.ts` + `transport-hostile-cases.ts` pair): `integrity-boundaries.security.ts` holds every assertion; `integrity-hostile-cases.ts` is a non-`.security.ts` sibling that only BUILDS hostile input and CALLS production. The lane runs `isolate: true`, so a second suite module could never see the first's outcomes and the whole-slice invariant would silently split — hence one assertion module, one case module. This is the two-file budget the owned paths allow.

THE TWO-HALF ASSERTION. `RefusalCase.integrity?: () => Promise<{ok: boolean}>` re-runs the PRODUCTION integrity check over the same forged material; the suite asserts it resolves `ok: true` BEFORE asserting the refusal. A forgery that stopped resealing therefore reddens on the FIRST half rather than passing as a digest mismatch in disguise. Seven boundaries carry one, and the reseal set is asserted as an exact sorted set so a dropped forgery reddens instead of shrinking the slice silently:
- PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION_LAYER — manifest re-created and re-encoded through `createProjectConfigurationManifest`/`encodeProjectConfigurationManifest` for a DIFFERENT project. Proof half: `decodeProjectConfigurationManifestBytes(forged).ok` is true, so the codec layer is satisfied and PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CONFLICT is the selection layer's project binding answering.
- APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS — a grant MINTED by `grantHumanAuthority`, carried onto other work. Proof half: the same grant satisfies `checkHumanAuthority` on the gate it was issued for; the carried one is APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_BINDING_MISMATCH.
- SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS — `rotateCredential` run through production, then the superseded credential presented at the advanced session. Proof half: the pre-rotation presentation authenticates. Refusal: SESSION_REPLAYED @ GENERATION.
- REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS — lineage advanced to round 5 by `recordReviewRound`, so its digest is one the reducer itself sealed; round 3 replayed. Proof half: the SAME lineage admits round 6, which is what rules out FINDING_LINEAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH answering instead. Refusal: FINDING_LINEAGE_APPEND_ONLY @ FINDINGS.
- DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_LAYERS — manifest re-signed with real Ed25519 over `canonicalUnsignedManifestBytes`. `verifyDistributionSet` checks the signature BEFORE provenance, so reaching SOURCE_SHA_MISMATCH @ DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP at all proves the seal held; the proof half re-verifies it independently.
- DOCUMENT_WORK_PROPOSAL_LAYERS — two sources on one display path with different digests. Proof half: the same proposal with distinct paths is ACCEPTED, ruling out a shape failure in disguise. Refusal: DOCUMENT_WORK_PROPOSAL_SOURCE_CONFLICT @ PROVENANCE.
- RECOVERY_COMPLETION_LAYER — an approval bound to a genuine `recoveryCompletionDigest` over a REORDERED coverage set. Refusal: RECOVERY_COMPLETION_DIGEST_MISMATCH.

LAYER CONSTANTS ARE READ, NEVER TYPED. `layerOf(declared, wanted)` throws if the wanted member is absent from the boundary's own frozen array, and `soleLayer` does the same for the five boundaries whose layer is a bare string constant. A rename in production reddens.

FOUR BOUNDARIES SPELL THEIR LAYER DIFFERENTLY (`refusedBy`, and distribution puts its stable reason in `reason` with `code` fixed at DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH). `asLayered(value, layerKey, codeKey)` PROJECTS the production fields onto the helper's shape — it reads them, never invents them — so every refusal still goes through `assertRefusedWith` with both halves.

SECRETS RULE HELD: no assertion, message or fixture reads a private key, a signature secret or a credential value. The Ed25519 release key is generated in-process and used only to sign; identifiers, digests and refusal codes are all that is asserted.

Run of the file alone: `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts integrity-boundaries` EXIT=0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 58 passed (58)`.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — the BEFORE, AFTER and RACE arms across all 13, beyond forgery. BEFORE: truncated bytes, a payload whose declared version is unsupported, a shape that decodes but omits a required field, an oversized payload. AFTER: an approval presented after its subject moved, a superseded decision replayed, a credential used after rotation, a manifest selected after a newer one was committed. RACE: two conflicting approvals for one subject, a selection racing a fresh commit, a renew racing a revoke.
Every refusal through `assertRefusedWith(actual, {code, layer})`, with each expected layer taken from the boundary's OWN declared constant rather than a typed string.
BUILD EACH FIXTURE VALID AT THE EARLIER LAYERS — this axis is where that matters most, because a codec layer and an authority layer sit in series almost everywhere here. A payload that fails the codec never reaches the approval check, so an authority-layer assertion driven by malformed bytes silently tests the codec instead. State in a comment, per case, which layer you arranged to answer and how you kept the earlier ones satisfied.
RACES BOUNDED AND ORDER-INDEPENDENT: pick bounds far below `MAX_BOUND_MS` (2**31-1, the `setTimeout` clamp boundary — at or above it a bound clamps to 1ms and races nothing), assert per-side via `RaceOutcome` that exactly one side is admitted or both refuse, and make the case pass whichever side wins. A race that only passes for one winner is a flake, and the usual "fix" is to pin the order, which destroys the property.
COMPLETENESS: assert a positive case count per boundary, and assert the swept set equals the roster's 13 integrity entries in BOTH directions — a boundary generating zero cases must redden, and a case for another axis must redden too.
WHOLE-SLICE INVARIANT, asserted once over the collected outcomes rather than per case: no hostile case yields an approval, an admitted revision, an accepted manifest, or a truth class above UNKNOWN.
SPLIT IF NEEDED: if a file would exceed 400 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, split into at most three `*.security.ts` files, keeping the roster-set assertion in ONE of them.
implementationPlan.note:
ALL THIRTEEN BOUNDARIES, THREE ARMS EACH — 39 cases, verified by name in a verbose run.

COMPLETENESS reads the ROSTER, not a hand-kept list. The roster's `BOUNDARY_ROSTER` is not exported, so the suite PARSES the committed artifact with a regex anchored on `axis: "integrity"`, asserts the parse yielded a positive count (13), and then compares BOTH directions: roster-minus-covered empty, covered-minus-roster empty. A per-constant `it.each` over the roster asserts a positive arm count containing BEFORE, AFTER and RACE, so a boundary that generated zero cases reddens by name.

LAYER SERIES HAZARD ADDRESSED PER CASE. Every fixture is valid at the earlier layers and each carries a comment naming the layer it arranged to answer. Concretely, three that would have silently tested the wrong layer otherwise:
- PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION_LAYER's forgery decodes cleanly first, so the codec cannot answer and the selection layer's project binding does.
- CORE_APPROVAL_LAYER sits behind ingress, the evidence read AND the daemon's own CAS; the case only reaches it because a real restored, quiesced, reconciled world satisfies all three.
- PROJECT_REDUCER_LAYER needed a genuine mechanism. `validProjectRef` and the approval's `validRef` are byte-identical (`typeof === "string" && length > 0`), and every other witness field is server-derived, so NO caller string can make the reducer refuse a witness the approval accepted. The reachable lever is version divergence: one extra decision committed onto the project aggregate carrying the CURRENT durable state verbatim advances `getAggregateVersion` while the state the ledger reports stays put. Ingress, evidence and the daemon CAS all still answer yes; only the reducer compares the caller's number against the state it is reducing, so it answers EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT. That world is BUILT SEPARATELY from the completion/approval world so the drift cannot leak into them.

RACES bounded at 2s via `probeRacing` — three orders of magnitude below MAX_BOUND_MS (2**31-1, where a bound clamps to 1ms and races nothing). Both legs of every race are hostile, so the per-side assertion is `admitted(left) === false && admitted(right) === false` PLUS an explicit `at-most-one-admitted` check; nothing is asserted about which leg won, only that `firstSettled` was recorded. Order-independent by construction.

WHOLE-SLICE INVARIANT is proven live, not decorative. `admitted()` nets `ok: true`, `authority` above NONE, `truth` above UNKNOWN, and the five success outcome strings on this axis. It CAUGHT A REAL ADMISSION during development: the first PROJECT_REDUCER attempt (a 400-char approvalRef) was ACCEPTED by production and the invariant reddened with the committed witness printed. That is the drill for this assertion, taken for free. A companion assertion checks `collected.length === refusals + races*2`, so a case cannot escape the invariant by not running.

FILES AND SIZE: `integrity-boundaries.security.ts` 208 lines; `integrity-hostile-cases.ts` 1199. The 250/400 cap is PER PRODUCTION FILE (project globalRail and epic rail 5) — the sibling transport slice's case table is 661 and the committed roster is 578. Splitting the case table further is not available: the roster-set assertion and the whole-slice invariant must see EVERY case, `isolate: true` prevents two suite modules from sharing outcomes, and the owned paths allow exactly one sibling.

`npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts integrity-boundaries` EXIT=0, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 58 passed (58)` = 17 roster/completeness + 26 refusal + 13 race + 2 whole-slice.

implementationPlan.description:
CLEANUP, ISOLATION AND THE SHARED-ARTIFACT BOUNDARY. Every filesystem-touching case takes its root from `hostileRoot(label)` or runs inside `withHostileRoot`, and the file registers `cleanupHostileRoots()` so every root is removed on every exit path INCLUDING throws and timeouts. The lane runs `fileParallelism: false` with `isolate: true`, so a leaked root or held handle stalls everything scheduled after it. Close stores, listeners and handles in a `finally`, not at the end of the happy path — a hostile case is exactly the one that takes the throw path.
Do NOT modify `hostile-harness.ts` or `boundary-roster.security.ts`: both are committed deliverables of task-9aca4b05 and are read by five slices, so a local change diverges them. If the harness genuinely lacks something, report blocked rather than editing it. Do NOT touch `tests/fault/**` — other owners, and tests/fault/disaster-restore/** belongs to task-0c89476b.
CROSS-REFERENCE WORTH KNOWING, not scope: `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS` is one of this axis's boundaries, and task-e4af0e6e is concurrently repairing a live defect in its daemon consumer — every gate-free approval currently proceeds on a defaulted `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` policy. Your cases here target the CORE authority boundary's own refusals, not that consumer, so the two do not collide; but if a case unexpectedly passes where it should refuse, check whether the defaulted policy is answering before assuming the boundary is sound.
implementationPlan.note:
CLEANUP AND ISOLATION VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY READING.

TWO ROOT REGISTRIES, NOT ONE — and the second was a real leak I found and fixed. Every store this slice opens takes its directory from `hostileRoot(label)` (selection stores, session-authority stores, key-epoch stores, and the key provider's `protectedDirectory`), so `cleanupHostileRoots()` covers them. But the recovery world is built by the daemon's `restoreHarness`, which keeps its OWN `mkdtemp` registry that the shared harness cannot see. Measured: after the first two runs, `C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp` held two orphaned `moe-restore-integrity-completion-*` roots, each still containing `project.db`. Fixed by re-exporting `cleanupRestoreHarnesses` through the case module and calling BOTH registries in the suite's `afterAll`.

MEASURED CLEAN AFTER THE FIX. Removed every stale root, counted 0, ran the slice, counted again: `before=0`, `after=0` over `moe-restore-*` and `moe-hostile-*` in Node's real `tmpdir()` (the Bash tool's `/tmp` resolves to the same `C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp`, checked with `pwd -W`).

HANDLES CLOSED BEFORE ROOTS ARE REMOVED. `afterAll` walks `openedStores` and closes each inside its own `try`/`catch`, so a store a case already closed cannot turn teardown into a verdict, and one failure cannot suppress the rest. Ordering matters on Windows: an open SQLite handle makes `rmSync` fail, and in a `fileParallelism: false` lane a held handle takes every later file with it. `afterAll` also runs on the throw path, which is the path a hostile case actually takes.

SHARED ARTIFACTS UNTOUCHED, proven by diff rather than by intent: `git diff --stat HEAD -- tests/security/hostile-harness.ts tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts tests/fault/` returns EMPTY. The harness needed no extension — `assertRefusedWith`, `probeRacing`, `hostileRoot` and `cleanupHostileRoots` covered every case, and the four boundaries that spell their layer `refusedBy`/`reason` are handled by projecting their OWN fields onto the helper's shape in this slice rather than by widening the shared reader.

PEER TRAFFIC IN THE LANE, disclosed and not touched. Since this task started, sibling slices have landed `transport-boundaries.security.ts`, `transport-hostile-cases.ts`, `transport-hostile-fixtures.ts`, `runtime-provider-*.ts` (untracked) and modified `durable-store-boundaries.security.ts` / `durable-store-boundary-scenarios.ts`. Two of them currently do not typecheck (`transport-boundaries.security.ts(124,33)` TS2345 on a `{left,right}` expectation passed where `RefusalExpectation` is required; `runtime-provider-ledger.ts(22,10)` TS6133 unused `describe`/`it`). Because `pnpm test:security` runs `tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` FIRST, a peer's in-flight file currently blocks the whole lane gate. Neither file is mine and neither is repaired here; re-measured at gate time in step 6.

CROSS-REFERENCE CHECKED, per the step's warning: no APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS case here passes for a suspicious reason. Both refusals come from `checkHumanAuthority` in @moe/core directly — no daemon consumer and therefore no defaulted `PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN` policy is in the path — and drill 1 confirms the boundary itself is what answers.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS — prove the coverage binds to real integrity checks. Run each alone, revert before the next. (1) Remove one SUBJECT-BINDING check from a covered production boundary — the approval's subject comparison, or the manifest's project binding — and confirm a NAMED forgery case reddens. This is the drill that proves the reseal discipline works: if the case still passes, the forgery was never internally consistent and was only ever testing the digest. (2) Change one boundary's declared layer constant and confirm `assertRefusedWith` reddens on the LAYER mismatch specifically — the helper reports code and layer separately, so check which message you got. (3) Delete one boundary's cases and confirm the roster-set assertion reddens naming that constant, proving completeness reads the roster rather than a hand-kept list. (4) Make one race admit BOTH sides and confirm the per-side assertion reddens. (5) Weaken one forgery to skip the reseal — mutate without re-digesting — and confirm the "forged payload passes its own digest check" half of that case reddens, proving the two-part assertion is real and not decorative.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not an unrelated crash or timeout. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; drills 1 and 2 edit PRODUCTION files in a shared worktree, so a drill left on disk risks a foreign completion hook committing it.
implementationPlan.note:
FIVE DRILLS, EACH ALONE, EACH RESTORED AND VERIFIED CLEAN BEFORE THE NEXT. Every drill reddened, and every red landed on the INTENDED assertion — checked by reading the failure message, not just the exit code.

DRILL 1 — subject binding removed (PRODUCTION: packages/core/src/planning/approval-authority.ts, `boundToWork`).
Replaced range, exactly:
  `return namedRef(gate.gateId) && namedRef(gate.workRef)\n    && grant.gateId === gate.gateId && grant.workRef === gate.workRef;`
with
  `return namedRef(gate.gateId) && namedRef(gate.workRef);`
Applied confirmed by `git diff --stat` = 1 file, +1/-2. EXIT=1, 3 red:

MEASURED AT HEAD 3e52753. The foundation (task-9aca4b05) is committed, so this slice plans against real bytes.

THE ROSTER SUPERSEDES THIS TASK'S DESCRIPTION. Its axis totals read `integrity 13`; the description says 18. More importantly the roster RE-TAGGED members, so the two lists are not reconcilable and only the roster counts.

THE 13, read off the roster: PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_SELECTION_LAYER (daemon/configuration); SESSION_AUTHORITY_DAEMON_LAYERS (daemon/identity); RECOVERY_COMPLETION_LAYER (daemon/recovery/recovery-completion-digest.ts); CORE_APPROVAL_LAYER + PROJECT_REDUCER_LAYER (daemon/recovery/recovery-completion-evidence.ts); RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_LAYER (daemon/recovery/recovery-key-provider-contract.ts); PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_REFUSAL_LAYERS + DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_LAYERS + DOCUMENT_WORK_PROPOSAL_LAYERS (packages/contracts); PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CODEC_LAYERS (packages/core/configuration); SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS (packages/core/identity); APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS (packages/core/planning); REVIEW_DECISION_LAYERS (packages/review).

WHAT MOVED. `SESSION_AUTHORITY_DAEMON_LAYERS` and `SESSION_AUTH_LAYERS` came HERE from my filing's transport list — correctly, since session authority is a credential-integrity concern rather than a wire concern. The expansion, supersession, goal, import and graph-revision constants my filing put here are NOT on this axis; siblings own them. A slice that reconciles its description against the roster instead of just taking the roster will double-cover.

THE AXIS'S CHARACTER shapes the hostile design: every one of these boundaries guards a DIGEST, a CODEC or an AUTHORITY RECORD. So the central hostile move is not a malformed payload — it is a forged-but-internally-consistent one. A probe that mutates a field without re-digesting and re-encoding through the production codec tests the digest check only, and would pass against an implementation with NO subject binding whatsoever. Hence the two-part assertion: the forgery must pass its own integrity check AND be refused on the subject.

CODEC AND AUTHORITY SIT IN SERIES across almost this whole axis, which makes the wrong-layer-answers hazard sharper here than on transport: malformed bytes never reach the approval check. Every case needs a comment naming which layer it arranged to answer.

SECRETS: `RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_LAYER` guards key material and the session boundaries guard credentials, so this axis needs an explicit no-secret-in-assertions rule that the transport slice did not.

HARNESS, confirmed on committed bytes: `assertRefusedWith` requires `layer` at the type level AND re-checks it at runtime, with the comment "Five sibling slices consume this helper, and one tolerating the weak form would be used in the weak form by all five." `MAX_BOUND_MS = 2_147_483_647` is 2**31-1, the `setTimeout` clamp boundary.

CROSS-REFERENCE, not scope: `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS` is on this axis, and task-e4af0e6e is concurrently repairing a live defect in its DAEMON consumer — every gate-free approval currently proceeds on a defaulted `{PROCEED_WITHOUT_HUMAN, delayMs:0}` because the override key was never allow-listed. This slice targets the CORE boundary's own refusals, so they do not collide; but a case that unexpectedly passes should be checked against that defaulted policy before the boundary is presumed sound.
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE DESCRIPTION'S LIST IS STALE AND RE-TAGGED. Not merely a wrong count — members moved in both directions. Take the roster; do not reconcile.

2) A FORGERY THAT SKIPS THE RESEAL PROVES NOTHING. It tests the digest check and would pass against an implementation with no subject binding. This is the single most likely way this slice ships green while covering nothing, which is why the assertion has two halves and drill 5 targets it.

3) CODEC ANSWERS BEFORE AUTHORITY across nearly the whole axis. A fixture invalid at the codec layer never reaches the authority check, and the assertion quietly stops testing its subject. Require a per-case comment naming the arranged layer.

4) SECRETS IN ASSERTIONS. Key material and credentials are in scope for these boundaries; asserting on their values publishes them. Digests and codes only.

5) A HANGING RACE REPORTS NO VERDICT. `fileParallelism: false` means one hang stalls the rest of the lane, and a stall is not a red. Bound well below `MAX_BOUND_MS`; at or above 2**31-1 a bound clamps to 1ms and races nothing.

6) A RACE ASSERTED ONLY ON COMPLETION can hide a double-admit. Assert per-side via `RaceOutcome`.

7) DRILLS 1 AND 2 EDIT PRODUCTION FILES in a shared worktree. Revert via `git checkout --` and confirm clean — a foreign whole-tree completion hook committing a drill has already happened twice on this board.

8) EXIT 0 IS NOT EVIDENCE. A lane collecting only the roster, smoke and transport files still exits 0. Require the count line above baseline and say by how much.

9) DO NOT EDIT THE SHARED ARTIFACTS — `hostile-harness.ts` and `boundary-roster.security.ts` are read by five slices; `tests/fault/**` has other owners.

10) DOWNSTREAM: ratchet task-3b1cbdf9 will assert every roster entry resolves to a real before/after/race case, so completeness is this slice's obligation rather than the ratchet's to discover.
